decisions.quote:
In this note, we replicate and extend Haglin et al. (2021), whose analysis ends in 2018. We find that
asymmetries in the association between Supreme Court approval and Americans’ ideological disagreement with the Court
have changed substantially and abruptly, depressing aggregate Supreme Court approval.
decisions.reason: The target original is unambiguously Haglin, Jordan, Merrill, and Ura (2021, online 2020; Political Research Quarterly 74(4): 955-969, DOI 10.1177/1065912920950482), which analyzed annual Gallup data from 2001 to 2018. Although the authors note a baseline computational reproduction of the 2001-2018 model estimates in Supplemental Materials Section 2, the primary empirical test reported in this research note uses new annual Gallup survey data from 2019 through 2024 (out-of-sample predictions for 2019-2024 and iterative seemingly unrelated regression models adding each new annual sample through 2024) to re-test whether the original ideological asymmetry in specific support for the Supreme Court persists. Because the study uses new post-2018 survey samples to re-test the previously published finding, both shipped and blind codings correctly classify the record type as 'replication'.
